sources.entry: Apostrophe - CMS with a focus on extensible in-context editing tools. (Demo, Source Code) MIT Nodejs

summary.one_liner: ApostropheCMS is an open-source, full-stack content management system built on Node.js and MongoDB that supports in-context editing on live pages and headless use with any frontend.
summary.what_it_does: Content creators can edit content directly on live pages instead of switching to a separate admin interface. Developers build sites with modern JavaScript on Node.js and store content in MongoDB. The CMS can also run headless, serving content through REST APIs to frameworks such as React, Vue, or Svelte. An Astro integration with starter kits is described for fetching content automatically. The README lists a CLI (@apostrophecms/cli) that generates a new project with a create command and a dev script. Pro extensions (paid) add advanced permissions, workflow, automated translation via DeepL, Google Translate or Azure, SEO and analytics, caching, and multisite management.
use_cases: build a website with in-context editing
headless CMS for a React, Vue, or Svelte frontend
manage content for a team of editors
notable: In-context editing directly on the live page
Headless mode with REST APIs usable from any frontend framework
Astro starter kits (Apollo and Essentials) named in the README
Pro extensions for permissions, workflow, and translation
caveats: Requires Node.js 20+ and MongoDB 6.0+ (Atlas or local install)
Advanced features such as granular permissions, workflow, automated translation and multisite are in paid Pro extensions
README gives no specific Pro pricing
